messages.subject: occuMulti predict versus predict ‘new’ interpretation.
parts:
occuMulti predict versus predict ‘new’ interpretation. 

 

Hello,

I have fit an occuMulti model on 5 co-occurring species, which has 2 detection parameters and 3 site-level covariates of interest. Using the top model (fit_M1), I use the ‘predict’ function to look at the species specific mean marginal occupancy:

 BAEA<-predict(fit_M1,'state', species=”BAEA”)[1,]

#Predicted         SE     lower     upper

#1 0.9546969 0.01118197 0.9292771 0.9698831

My understanding of this output is that these are the predictions across all possible occupancy states (0000, 1000, 1100, etc.) at each possible site (taking into account each site's covariate values) along with standard errors. This is marginalized across all species in the model. Note that the marginal mean occupancy for Bald Eagle is high (0.95, range 0.92-0.97).

 I also look at the marginal effect of each covariate (e.g. below for latitude)

nd_marg <- data.frame(

  year_st = rep(mean(occ_covs$year_st), 100),

  longitude = rep(mean(occ_covs$longitude), 100),

  latitude = seq(min(occ_covs$latitude), max(occ_covs$latitude),length.out = 100))

marg <- predict(fit_M1, type = 'state', species = “BAEA”, newdata = nd_marg)

The predicted marginal occupancy for BAEA based on the covariate latitude range from 0.58-0.89, marginalized across all other species. I notice that in all cases the predicted marginal occupancy values for the covariate effects (using a new dataframe for each) are below the predicted mean marginal occupancy values (0.95), and fall well outside the confidence intervals (0.92-0.96). I am having a hard time articulating why this would be the case. I suspect this is because the predictive power of a single covariate is less than the predictive power of the full model that takes into consideration each site covariate value? But why such a large difference?

Is there a sync way to explain why this is the case?

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: occuMulti predict versus predict ‘new’ interpretation.
parts:
Is the predicted marginal occupancy of BAEA at site 1, which is calculated based on the specific covariate values for site 1. You don't show these specific covariate values but they are likely the reason for what you are seeing.

When you calculate the marginal effects of covariates like this, you are holding all covariates except one at their mean values. So all predictions for all marginal plots are derived from sets of covariate values that are uniformly "average" except for one covariate which ranges from very low to very high. Now, suppose that site 1 represents an extreme case and has "very high" values of all or most covariates, relative to the averages across sites. In your case perhaps it's in the upper corner of the map and so has both high latitude and high longitude. That would result in a prediction which could (depending on the exact model) fall well outside any of the predictions generated when you were holding all non-focal covariates at their means.

If you are not sure about this, plug the actual covariate values for site 1 into the newdata. You should get the same results (the CIs might not be exactly identical because they are bootstrapped).

Ken
